title: PostgreSQL timeout / connection-pressure signals
description: Patterns identifying PostgreSQL statement timeouts, connection timeouts, pool exhaustion, and deadlocks — all visible in postgres / pgbouncer / app logs.

patterns.name: statement_timeout triggered
patterns.explanation: PostgreSQL cancelled a statement because it exceeded the configured execution limit.
patterns.severityRationale: Warning because the query failed, while the database may remain available to other work.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Known slow reports and deliberately bounded queries can hit an intentional timeout.

patterns.name: connection timeout
patterns.explanation: A client or pool could not establish a PostgreSQL connection in time.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because connection failure can prevent the application from reaching its primary datastore.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Failover drills, cold starts, and temporary pool saturation can cause transient timeouts.

patterns.name: too many connections
patterns.explanation: PostgreSQL refused a connection because the configured connection limit was exhausted.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because new application work cannot reach the database until capacity is restored.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Load tests and planned connection-limit exercises can intentionally trigger this condition.

examples.positive: FATAL: too many connections for role app

patterns.name: deadlock detected
patterns.explanation: PostgreSQL detected a transaction deadlock and aborted work to break the cycle.
patterns.severityRationale: Critical because concurrent writes are conflicting and at least one transaction was terminated.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Expected high-contention workflows may occasionally deadlock and rely on retry logic.

patterns.name: canceling statement due to lock timeout
patterns.explanation: PostgreSQL cancelled a statement after it waited too long for a lock.
patterns.severityRationale: Warning because one operation failed while the database can continue serving other work.
patterns.falsePositiveNote: Short lock budgets in normal concurrency control can create expected cancellations.

examples.positive: canceling statement due to lock timeout
